sense: measuring a lot from side to side

evidence: Mart. 13.81.1: quamvīs lāta gerat patella rhombum
Caes. BG 7.19.1: nōn lātior pedibus quīnquāgintā
terms.comment: The width is lātitūdō: in lātitūdinem patēre, to extend in width (Caes. BG 1.2.5).

evidence: Liv. 21.35.8: unde longē ac lātē prōspectus erat

phrases.latin: quamvīs lāta gerat patella rhombum, rhombus lātior est tamen patellā
phrases.english: however wide the dish that holds the turbot, the turbot is still wider than the dish

phrases.latin: hunc ex omnibus ferē partibus palūs difficilis atque impedīta cingēbat nōn lātior pedibus quīnquāgintā
phrases.english: on almost every side it was surrounded by a difficult, treacherous marsh, no more than fifty feet wide

sources: Lewis & Short: latus · Lewis & Short: late · Lewis & Short: amplus
